newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent firmer, but remains cautious.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent firmer, but remains cautious.

text.p: Brent crude futures prices were firmer on Thursday in Asia but sentiment remained cautious after two successive days of fresh 13-month lows.
July Brent was last traded on SIMEX at $17.45 per barrel -- on just five lots -- up 10 cents from London overnight.
London ended down 15 cents at $17.35 and just three cents above after the intraday low -- the lowest level since May 20, 1996.
NYMEX July crude was also weaker overnight, falling 14 cents to $18.53.
Prices rebounded slightly on ACCESS during Asian hours and July was last traded at $18.62, up nine from New York.
Brokers said sentiment remained cautious about a rebound after London failed to make much headway on the upside overnight.
However, they said the next major low on the charts was $16.75 -- the low of May 20, 1996. Since that was some distance away, it might tempt players to cut back short positions ahead of the weekend.
